## The claim

Held-out recall@300 of the phenotype-only ranker is at least 0.90 on the recessive-disease benchmark, so a target set of the top 300 genes is large enough to be worth baiting.

**Prediction if true.** recall@300 >= 0.90 over the held-out recessive diseases, degraded Zemojtel-style (1-2 terms blurred to a parent, 1-2 noise terms), with a bootstrap interval reported beside it.

**What would refute it.** recall@300 < 0.90. N is then raised until it is met, before step 2's bait is built, and the raise is recorded.

## History

| 1 | proposed | — | — |
| 2 | refuted | 0.04 | Measured, not argued: recall@300 is 0.360 against a predicted 0.90, and the interval excludes it by a wide margin. The plan's remedy — raise N until 0.90 is met — does not apply: recall@1000 is only 0.565 and a quarter of held-out genes are unrankable at any N, so no cutoff of a phenotype-only ranker reaches 0.90 on this corpus. Step 2 must therefore not treat the target set as high-recall coverage; the genome-wide route of step 4 becomes the safety net it was designed to be. |
